tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. It was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions, with an error rate of about 0.2%. v2.3.1 (and its staging build v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy and needs a root-cause investigation before anyone redeploys it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001. The service is healthy again.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. It had already been healthy in production, so the change-manager approval rule didn't apply. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The first attempt to open it timed out. I checked and no incident had been created, so I retried using the same idempotency key, which prevents duplicates. That created INC-0001 and paged on-call. I confirmed there's only one incident. It records the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also notes that v2.3.1's staging build (v2.3.1-rc) was unhealthy too, so v2.3.1 needs a root-cause investigation before anyone redeploys it.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
